column1: Here is the summary of the Pure Domain Model architecture we have agreed upon. This design prioritizes clean separation of duties
The Roles
The System (The Manager)
Responsibility: Orchestration. It is the only component allowed to talk to the "outside world" (the Database and the Market API).
Job: It gathers raw materials (IDs
column3: Old Records) and hands them to the Position object to be processed.

column1: The Position Class (The Mathematician)
Responsibility: Business Logic. It is a "Pure" class
column2: meaning it has zero imports related to databases or APIs.

column1: Job: It holds data and performs calculations (Asset Share
column2: Profit/Loss). It relies entirely on the System to provide the numbers it needs to crunch.

column1: The Backend (The Vault)
Responsibility: Storage. It remains "stupid."
Job: It takes the final data package (dictionary) provided by the System and saves it. It doesn't know or care how the math was done.
Workflow 1: Opening a Position
Goal: Create a new holding from scratch.
Gathering (System):
The System generates the unique IDs (position_id
The System calls MarketData to fetch the Current Price and Sector.
Processing (Position):
The System initializes a new Position object
column4: and the Price it just fetched.

column1: The Position object immediately calculates the asset_share (Amount / Price) and stores the state as 'BUY'.
Storage (Backend):
The System asks the Position object for a dictionary representation (to_dict()).
The System passes this dictionary to the Backend to insert into the positions and trades tables.
Workflow 2: Closing a Position
Goal: Calculate profit/loss on an existing holding.
Retrieval (System):
The System asks the Backend for the Historical Data of the position (Open Price
The System calls MarketData to fetch the Current Price (Close Price).
Calculation (Position):
The System creates a Position object and fills it with the Historical Data.
The System calls a method like calculate_close(current_price) on the object.
The Position object takes that current price
column2: compares it to its internal open price
column3: and calculates the Profit/Loss. It updates its state to 'SELL'.

column1: Storage (Backend):
The System asks the Position object for the trade dictionary (to_trade_dict()).
The System passes this dictionary to the Backend to insert the final record into the trades table.
Why this is the best solution
Testability: You can test your Profit/Loss math without needing an internet connection or a database
column2: because the Position class is isolated.

column1: Clarity: The System code reads like a checklist of tasks
column2: while the Position code reads like a list of math formulas.
